title: FF6-style graphic fidelity that looks good on all screens

posts.author: StephBells
posts.body:
Hi friends!
I want my graphics to be 16x16 to keep the retro look of the SNES. I don't want too much of the map revealed or the characters too small. I need the 48x48 tiles of MZ because most plugins use that, and I can't code. I need those plugins. I need the game to fit all screens with no black bars. I need this to apply to everything, from characters to UI.
What are my most favorable options, even if I have to pay for them?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
StephBells said:
I need the game to fit all screens
Click to expand...
The answer is none.
For aspect ratios, you'd have to adjust how many tiles the camera can see (the resolution). That might be possible and is the least technical hurdle to overcome, but the second is that screen resolutions vary. It is impossible to pick a resolution that will scale perfectly to every screen resolution.
Someone, somewhere is going to have a screen that will use a non-integer value to fit the game to the screen (or otherwise letter/pillar box it to scale it to the largest integer)
The only way to overcome this is:
A) make multiple versions of your assets for different resolution scales, then have a plugin detect and change to the correct asset - an absolutely massive task in the art department.
Or
B ) completely rewrite how the engine handles graphics so that it can utilize vector art. Which is not only going to be difficult from a technical standpoint, but also demanding reworking of all visual assets to fit the new require file format.
If you are just starting to make your game, I highly recommend you put aside perfecting nit-picked visuals such as pillar/letter boxing and non-integer scaling and instead focus your efforts on just making a good game. People can look past a game not scaling well if the game itself is good, but people will have a hard time looking past a bad game even if it scales perfectly to their monitor.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I recommend setting a resolution that scales well with 1080p/4k monitors. The chart in the link below shows some possible resolutions. You should look at the last row in the chart.
Basically, a base resolution of 640×360 will provide the most compatibility with common screen's since the most common aspect ratio is 16:9 (640x360 is a 16:9 ratio) and will multiply to common resolutions easily; 720p, 1080p, 1440p, and 4k.
This is probably the easiest and least complicated way of ensuring the art is displayed cleanly on a wide set of screens. It does have some short comings;
Many laptop screens use a 16:10 or 3:2 aspect ratio. Most laptops use some ratio that can display a 1080p/1440p/4k image without problem (meaning it will scale properly), but it will have letter boxing.
The Steam Deck uses a 1280x800 screen which is neither the same aspect ratio nor is it an integer of the proposed base resolution of 640x360.
Some PC users use ultra-wide screen monitors that are 21:9 (or even higher). While it will likely scale properly to fit the ultra-wide monitor, it will have pillar boxes
The way RPG Maker MV/Z handles full-screening is that it will fit the image to the screen, regardless of the resolution of the monitor. This means that it
will
attempt to scale the image to non-integer values while prioritizing the ratio (so the image doesn't become stretched). This will cause pixels to look a little bit blurry.
While I don't know any publicly available plugins, Omori - an RPG Maker MV game - changed the behavior of the full-screen option in RM, where it locked the image size to only integer values.
I believe, in combination with the suggested base resolution, this would be the most practical approach to cover
most
monitors.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
StephBells said:
I want my graphics to be 16x16 to keep the retro look of the SNES.
Click to expand...
You're starting from a faulty premise. The "retro look" has nothing to do with how large the graphics are, it has to do with how they're drawn.
Anything that's equally pixelated - that is, has large enough blocks of color - will look like SNES graphics.
Playing the original FF6 on an emulator and leaving it the original size would be extremely annoying, trying to peer at graphics that small. I've resized Zsnesw up to a reasonable size on my monitor, and you can see the sprites and tiles there are actually
larger
than in MZ, but they still look perfectly good and maintain their visual style.
The only thing that basing your art on 16x16 squares accomplishes is making them
really small
on modern displays.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
StephBells said:
My objective is to scale them threefold, but I wasn't sure if it's better to do it beforehand or in the game itself with a plugin, and if a plugin could actually do that in a non-destructive way.
Click to expand...
I don't know what you mean by "destructive," but there's no reason to make the game do constant resizing every time it draws a sprite - just make the images larger. Then you don't have to worry about how it interacts with UI elements, animations, balloons, whatever.
You can draw at 16x16 and scale it up or just start with a larger canvas in the first place and make your brush sized 3x3.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Yeah, use upscaled graphics.
Don't use permanent zoom plugins. They will limit you more than you can imagine beforehand.
ATT_Turan said:
You can draw at 16x16 and scale it up or just start with a larger canvas in the first place and make your brush sized 3x3.
Click to expand...
Stick with drawing on 16x16.
If you draw with a 3x3px brush, you'll end up doing "illegal" pixel placement like this.
